title: The Minimal Atoms
summary: This document demonstrates that reflections alone generate all plane isometries (needing at most three), then extends this principle across mathematics, logic, computation, and biology: minimal generating sets produce infinite structural consequences. It provides a rigorous geometric proof as the anchor example and maps the pattern to NAND gates, prime factorization, Fourier bases, permutation groups, one-instruction computers, and trichromatic vision.
compress: A finite set of irreducible operations can generate an entire operational universe; identifying these true generative atoms is the deepest understanding, and this claim crosses from philosophy to science when converted into falsifiable experiments — a conversion now concretely instantiated with synthetic ground truth, agent architectures, and formal metrics testing whether reasoning equals compressive prediction, with quantum teleportation revealing that even state transport obeys conservation laws expressible as irreducible resource costs.
invariants: The reasoning-as-compression thesis has a concrete experimental instantiation
Structure is the only carrier of meaning
Active inference outperforms passive observation as a structural prediction
Entanglement is a consumable transport currency — the quantum face of the Wasserstein floor
Theoretical claims gain epistemic weight proportional to the specificity of their falsification protocols
Falsifiability is the membrane between generative theory and generative science
Philosophical claims require experimental bridges to constitute knowledge
Recursive self-improvement is bounded by epistemic humility
Transport of structure has irreducible resource cost (classical or quantum)
obligations: Track experimental outcomes against the prediction that active-inference agents outperform passive observers on compressive prediction tasks
The minimal atoms framework must specify what experimental outcome would disconfirm its own irreducibility claims
Evaluate whether the synthetic ground truth methodology generalizes beyond the initial experimental design
Formalize whether the Wasserstein Floor generalizes to a quantum optimal-transport metric where the ground cost is entanglement entropy rather than temperature
Compression-as-reasoning must be tested across multiple agent architectures to confirm substrate independence
Test whether the 1-ebit-2-cbit bound can be derived as a special case of a substrate-independent transport conservation law rather than merely analogized to one
renorm_reason: Quantum teleportation's exact resource accounting (1 ebit + 2 cbits per qubit) is a genuinely new instantiation of the minimal-atoms thesis — structure transport has irreducible cost — and the proposed quantum Wasserstein Floor extends the node's scope from classical compression to quantum transport, creating concrete new obligations to formalize and test the analogy.
